ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows two animals moving on a circular stadium track; the key numerical information comes from the problem statement. Treat the stadium as a closed track with circumference 330 m, and represent positions modulo 330. Roo jumps 2 m per second and stops after 25 seconds, so the position where Roo stops is 2×25=50 m. Suppose t seconds have elapsed from the start, then Kanga's position is 5t mod 330. After Roo stops, for Kanga to be beside Roo again, it is necessary that 5t ≡ 50 (mod 330), and t>25. Dividing both sides by 5 gives t ≡ 10 (mod 66). The smallest such t greater than 25 is 76 seconds. Therefore, after Roo stops at 25 seconds, it still has to wait 76−25=51 seconds.

Kanga's position after total time t seconds is 5t modulo 330. To be beside Roo after Roo has stopped, solve 5t ≡ 50 mod 330 with t>25. Divide by 5 to get t ≡ 10 mod 66, so the next valid total time is t=76 seconds. The additional time after Roo stops is 76−25=51 seconds.

method.method_draft: Reason from the instant Roo stops. From the text, after 25 seconds Roo is 50 m from the start and Kanga is 125 m from the start. Since they move in the same direction and Roo is now fixed, Kanga must continue around the track from 125 m to Roo's stopped position at 50 m. Along the forward direction this distance is 330−(125−50)=255 m. Kanga covers 5 m each second, so the time needed is 255÷5=51 seconds.
method.CoT_raw: The image shows an oval stadium track with two kangaroos moving around it, matching the text description. Reason from the instant Roo stops. After 25 seconds, Roo has traveled 25 × 2 = 50 m from the start, and Kanga has traveled 25 × 5 = 125 m from the start. Roo is now fixed at the 50 m position. Kanga must keep moving forward around the 330 m perimeter from position 125 m back around to position 50 m. The forward distance is 330 - (125 - 50) = 330 - 75 = 255 m. Since Kanga jumps 5 m each second, the time needed is 255 ÷ 5 = 51 seconds.
